record.final_answer:
No. As far as I can find, there are no published numbers for that setup.

The only published figure is the **Marrowlog 2.4 performance report** (https://marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2, 18 June 2026). It shows one agent shipping **180,000 lines/s on 1 vCPU**, but the test doesn't match how we'd run it:

| | Report | Our agents (`README.md`, `config/agent.yaml`) |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | Plain TCP, no TLS in any run | TLS (the planned switch) |
| Line size | 200 bytes or less | About 900 bytes on average (JSON with stack traces) |
| Disk buffer | Off | Off (matches) |
| `batch_lines` | 500 | 500 (matches) |
| CPU | 1 vCPU | 1 vCPU reserved (matches) |

The report itself says TLS, lines over 200 bytes and the disk buffer were not measured. That means 180k lines/s doesn't tell us whether we'd reach 50k lines/s per agent. Our lines are about 4.5× longer, and TLS adds per-byte encryption cost, so the plain-TCP figure probably overstates what we'd get. The two effects compound, and we don't know by how much.

The maintainers said they'd measure TLS in a Q4 report, but it isn't out yet (`/perf/2026-q4` returns 404). An earlier session reached the same conclusion, and the report still says the same.

**Recommendation:** don't wait for Q4. The security deadline is the end of next quarter, so benchmark it ourselves. Run one agent on 1 vCPU with `tls: true` and a replay of real ~900-byte lines against a test collector, and check whether it holds 50k lines/s. Measure CPU headroom too, not just whether it keeps up. If it's tight, adjusting `batch_lines` or giving the agent a second vCPU are the obvious levers. I can draft the test config if you'd like.
